back: Crops and livestock on the same farm, supporting each other (residues feed animals; manure and draught power serve crops).
Growing one crop only, often on the same land every season.
Two or more crops grown at the same time on the same land in a definite pattern, e.g. alternate rows.
Two or more crops grown together at the same time with no definite pattern.
Intensive: high inputs and output per hectare on a small area. Extensive: large area, low inputs and output per hectare.
Subsistence: mainly to feed the family. Commercial: mainly for sale at a profit.
Pest, disease and weed build-up; falling fertility; all income depends on one crop.
Higher total output, nitrogen from legumes, better ground cover, less risk; but crops compete and mechanisation is harder.
Yield (kg/ha) = total harvest (kg) ÷ area (ha); 1 t/ha = 1,000 kg/ha.
